sam.belief: Sam remains the only person who reports seeing a tall shape beside Reservoir Road after his bus route. He cannot identify it.
sam.stance: He keeps The Tall One as a cautious description. He finds Roadside Shape and Unidentified Tall Shape more like labels than names people would say.

harold.belief: Harold has not seen anything and is skeptical that Sam can identify what he saw.
harold.stance: He continues to favor Roadside Shape as a practical description based on Sam's account, without claiming what the shape was. He thinks The Tall One sounds too settled.

ellen.belief: Ellen has not seen anything and wants evidence before accepting an identification.
ellen.stance: She continues to favor Unidentified Tall Shape because it preserves uncertainty. She finds The Tall One too informal and Roadside Shape incomplete as terminology.

public_record.headline: Sam Evers proposes "The Tall One" as name for reservoir animal
Harold Vale and Ellen Price dispute Sam Evers' proposed name
Reservoir animal naming debate draws community comment

turns.text: Sam, why The Tall One?
It says what I could make out, and no more.
It says what you made out. That isn't quite the same as saying what was there.
Precisely. A description should not quietly become an identification.
I meant it as a name, not a report on its nature.
Then I object to the word 'the.' It sounds settled.
The article is grammatical. It does not certify a specimen.
So the disagreement is partly about grammar?
Grammar matters when a name is going on a notice.
There is no notice, Harold.
Three names are now in circulation. Sam, does The Tall One still suit you?
Yes. It is short, and I only mean it to describe what I could make out.
Roadside Shape is shorter than Ellen's, and it says where the account places it.
It says roadside, but not which road. I prefer the full uncertainty in Unidentified Tall Shape.
That sounds like a heading on a file, not something a person would call it.
A file heading can be useful. We have no reason to make the wording more certain.
I didn't ask anyone to decide what it was. I wanted a name I could say plainly.
And I want one that doesn't imply the description is a settled identification.
Then we agree on the caution and disagree on the paperwork.
For tonight, all three proposals remain proposals.
We have no new proposal tonight. Is that a relief to anyone?
It gives Roadside Shape a fair chance to be considered without another entry crowding the page.
There is no page, Harold. And consideration does not require a queue.
I still say The Tall One plainly. That's useful when you are talking, not filing.
Roadside Shape would fit on a notice and doesn't say what it was.
It leaves out that the account describes it as tall. That is not a small omission.
Unidentified Tall Shape is careful, but I would have to take a breath halfway through.
A breath is not a defect in a term.
And none of you is speaking from having seen it, except Sam.
Correct. I am arguing over the wording of his account.
